topPRs.title: Add timeout to vm-runner
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**
Adds a configurable timeout for VM execution in the run-trace command to prevent the runner from hanging indefinitely if the VM hangs.

Changes:
- Add --vm-timeout CLI flag to run-trace command with a default of 3 hours. Set to 0 to disable timeout.
- Apply timeout context in runOnce() before creating the trace provider
- ~~Add timeouts_total metric to track timeout occurrences~~ (removed)
- ~~Logs timeout specifically (as opposed to panic or failure)~~(removed)


**Tests**

- `TestNewRunnerSetsTimeout` - verifies the timeout is stored in the Runner
- `TestRunOnceAppliesTimeout` - verifies the context deadline is applied when timeout is set, and not applied when timeout is zero
- `TestRunOnceReturnsTimeoutError` - verifies that a slow trace provider causes context.DeadlineExceeded to be returned

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: add test to base gate for unsafe gossip / head progression
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
We recently realised that acceptance tests do not give us good coverage for unsafe head progression via p2p gossip. See, for example, https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/17940 (a bug which wasn't caught by ATs) as well as a recent op-reth bug we only caught on devnet. 

This test adds that coverage, and simply asserts that a) there are some non-sequencer verifier nodes and b) they catch up to the sequencer within a timeout period. 

The test disables the sysgo batcher, because otherwise safe chain derivation would allow the test to pass even if gossip was broken. Therefore this test should not run against external networks. 

I confirmed manually that introducing a bug, where op-node just rejects gossip payloads unconditionally, does indeed cause this test to fail.

topPRs.title: Remove go 1.24 feature flag, leaving SysGetRandom syscall enabled
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

This removes the `SupportWorkingSysGetRandom` feature flag, leaving `SysGetRandom` support enabled, because Cannon version 8 has shipped and go 1.24 is now supported.

It could make sense to leave empty `getNoopSyscalls64()` and `getSupportedSyscalls()`, for the next time. I chose to clean them up, but let me know if you think we should keep them.
